newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower in line with Australian unit.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower in line with Australian unit.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed lower in active trade on Wednesday as both it and the Australian dollar ran into selling.
The Kiwi finished at US$0.6946/53 and 68.38 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6967/74 and 68.54 at the opening.
A Wellington dealer said selling had been mainly out of Asia, and Japanese banks in particular were sellers of Australian dollars.
But he said support had kicked in around US$0.7735-45 for the Aussie and 0.6950 for the Kiwi, with exporter interest, TWI-buying and various shorts buying back the currency.
An Auckland dealer described the New Zealand dollar as "heavy".
"The dollar has come off its highs and our interest rates have gone up, but the currency's also drifted down, so there's not what you'd call too many bulls out there at this stage," he said.
Local exporters had been picking away around the 0.6950 level, but not in huge volumes, and there was potential for a retreat towards 0.6920 overnight, the dealer said.
